newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat to lower.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bond prices lost modest morning strength to end flat to slightly lower, but firm pricing was seen on Wednesday's two big deals, New York City and Massachusetts, market sources said.
"I'd say (prices) are unchanged to off 1/8 of a point maybe, just more or less treading water," one trader said. "It had a better tone this morning, but it just sort of petered out here."
High-grade issues were unmoved Wednesday, an analyst said. Dollar bonds, which had opened slightly stronger, closed slightly weaker, he said.
"They weren't even up 1/8, and, when they went down, they weren't down 1/8," the analyst said.
The dollar bond fade occurred in the afternoon, in sympathy with Treasury market weakness, he said.
"I have a feeling the Treasury auction wasn't so good," the analyst said.

The government sold $10 billion of 10-year notes at an average yield of 6.273 percent with a one basis point tail. Some government traders said while results were in line with estimates, the market had built up expectations for stronger demand.
The Treasury is scheduled to sell $10 billion of 30-year bonds Thursday.

The 30-year benchmark bond closed down 13/32 at 101-23/32 to yield 6.62 percent. In debt futures, the December municipal contract closed down 11/32 at 116-8/32. The December T-bond contract closed down 5/32 at 113-20/32. The MOB spread was 84 ticks.
Turning to new issues, a municipal analyst described pricing on the New York City and Massachusetts deals as "firm."
"New York, they bumped some a little bit in kind of the middle of their loan, and they eased by an 02 in a couple of others, in the longer end," the analyst said. "It probably came out as a wash."

Bear Stears & Co said it repriced $834 million New York City general obligation bond offering, raising the top yield in 2026 to 6.20 percent from 6.18 percent. Bear Stearns also won $136 million taxable portion of New York City's deal, winning the offering with a true interest cost bid of 6.506 percent.
As for Massachusetts, Ken Olshansky, the states' deputy treasurer, said it increased to deal's size to $923 million from $700 million because of favorable market conditions.

"For the most part, it looks like deals are getting done at relatively aggressive levels," a municipal trader said. "You've got to remember munis have underperformed for such a long time they are attractive."
Turning to Thursday's new issues, negotiated issues are expected to number 14 and total $414 million. On the competitive side, 19 sales are expected totaling $216 million.
